title: Callvale after: the jobs table in DynamoDB
claim: Pipeline steps read and write each job by call ID in the jobs table, and the dashboard lists jobs through the index by-customer.
alt: After: the S3 upload event starts the start-job function, which starts the state machine call-pipeline. Each step reads and writes the job item by call ID in the DynamoDB table jobs. The dashboard queries the global secondary index by-customer. Time to live removes old job items.

edges.label: starts
edges.say: The start-job function starts the state machine call-pipeline for each upload.

edges.label: by call ID
edges.say: Each step reads and writes the job item by its call ID in the jobs table.

edges.label: by customer
edges.say: The dashboard lists one customer's jobs through the global secondary index by-customer.

edges.label: deletes old
edges.say: Time to live deletes old job items without consuming any write throughput.

notes: Brief 28 story pair, after (pipeline state P3); 2-deep.md#decision-record (after Decision). Title, claim, alt and steps from brief.json. Same cells as dynamodb-before for uploads, start-job, the pipeline and the dashboard (B2); the table group replaces RDS Proxy and PostgreSQL. Step 4 fact: dynamodb-faq-ttl-no-write-throughput; steps 1 to 3 are story. No second Region (stage 4). No number drawn.
